questions.prompt: Which numeral is six hundred thousand, nine hundred and four?
questions.explanation: Six hundred thousand plus nine hundred plus four is 600,904.

questions.prompt: What is 11 × 14?
questions.explanation: Eleven groups of 14 equal 154.

questions.prompt: Which fraction shows five of twelve equal parts?
questions.explanation: The numerator counts five selected parts and the denominator counts twelve equal parts.

questions.prompt: An equilateral triangle has side length 9 cm. What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: Three equal sides of 9 cm total 27 cm.

questions.prompt: What time is 50 minutes before 1:25 pm?
questions.explanation: Subtract 25 minutes to noon, then 25 more to reach 12:35 pm.

questions.prompt: A box contains 9 rows of 13 beads. How many beads are there?
questions.explanation: Nine times 13 equals 117.

questions.prompt: Which decimal is closest to 1?
questions.explanation: The distances from 1 are 0.04, 0.11, 0.18 and 0.25, so 0.96 is closest.

questions.prompt: A rectangle has perimeter 30 cm and width 5 cm. What is its length?
questions.explanation: Half the perimeter is 15 cm; subtract the width to get a 10 cm length.

questions.prompt: How many degrees are in three right angles?
questions.explanation: Each right angle is 90°, so three total 270°.

questions.prompt: A jar is 5/8 full with 45 marbles. How many marbles fit when it is full?
questions.explanation: One eighth is 45 ÷ 5 = 9, so eight eighths is 72.

questions.prompt: A ferry carries 238 passengers, then 79 leave and 46 board. How many passengers are aboard?
questions.explanation: After 79 leave, 159 remain; adding 46 gives 205.

questions.prompt: Which multiplication gives a product between 300 and 350?
questions.explanation: Seventeen times 19 is 323, which lies between 300 and 350.

metadata.subject: numeracy
metadata.skill: Locate a product in an interval

questions.prompt: Which is the most reasonable capacity of a drink bottle?
questions.explanation: A personal drink bottle commonly holds several hundred millilitres.

questions.prompt: A number has six factors: 1, 2, 4, 7, 14 and itself. What is the number?
questions.explanation: The missing final factor paired with 1 is 28; all listed values divide 28.

metadata.subject: numeracy
metadata.skill: Infer a number from its factors

questions.prompt: A chart records 24 fiction, 16 information and 10 poetry books. What percentage are poetry books?
questions.explanation: There are 50 books; 10 out of 50 is one fifth, or 20%.
Align decimal places: 3.25 + 0.80 + 1.06 = 5.11.

questions.prompt: Which number becomes 63,000 when rounded to the nearest thousand?
questions.explanation: 63,482 is below 63,500, so it rounds to 63,000.

questions.prompt: A car uses 7.5 L of fuel for each 100 km. How much does it use for 300 km?
questions.explanation: Three lots of 100 km use 3 × 7.5 = 22.5 L.

questions.prompt: A bag has 4 yellow, 6 black and 10 white tiles. Which colour has probability 3/10?
questions.explanation: There are 20 tiles and 6/20 simplifies to 3/10, so black fits.

metadata.skill: Match a probability to a category

questions.prompt: A stall earned $485 on Saturday and $369 on Sunday, then paid $275 in costs. What remained?
questions.explanation: The earnings total $854; subtracting $275 leaves $579.

questions.prompt: Which statement is true of every rhombus?

options.text: Only one pair of sides is parallel
Its diagonals are equal in length

questions.explanation: A rhombus is defined by four equal sides; the other properties are not always true.

questions.prompt: A sequence starts 2, 6, 14, 30. Each term is double the previous term plus 2. What is the next term?
questions.explanation: Double 30 to get 60, then add 2 to get 62.

questions.prompt: The data are 4, 7, 7, 9, 13, 14. What is the mode?
questions.explanation: Seven occurs twice and every other value occurs once.

questions.prompt: A prism is built from 4 layers, each containing 6 rows of 5 cubes. How many cubes are used?
questions.explanation: Each layer has 30 cubes and four layers have 120.

questions.prompt: A printer makes 48 pages each minute for 17 minutes. How many pages does it print?
questions.explanation: Ten minutes gives 480 pages and seven gives 336; together that is 816.

questions.prompt: Nine lengths of 375 mm are joined. What total length is made in millimetres?
questions.explanation: Nine times 375 equals 3,375.
questions.instructions: Write just the number of millimetres, without the unit.

questions.prompt: Eight identical bowls hold 6 kg of fruit altogether. How many grams are in each bowl?
questions.explanation: Six kilograms is 6,000 g; 6,000 ÷ 8 = 750.
questions.instructions: Write just the number of grams, without the unit.

questions.prompt: A rectangle has area 96 m². Its length is 12 m. What is its width?
questions.explanation: Width equals area divided by length: 96 ÷ 12 = 8.
questions.instructions: Write just the number of metres, without the unit.

questions.prompt: A club raised $3,600. It spent $875 on equipment and $649 on transport. How many dollars remained?
questions.explanation: The costs total 1,524 dollars; 3,600 − 1,524 = 2,076.
questions.instructions: Write just the number of dollars, without the unit.

questions.prompt: A quarter of a collection is 19 shells. How many shells are in three quarters?
questions.explanation: One quarter is 19, so three quarters is 3 × 19 = 57.

questions.prompt: A clock gains 3 minutes every 2 hours. How many minutes will it gain in 14 hours?
questions.explanation: Fourteen hours contains seven 2-hour periods, and 7 × 3 = 21.
questions.instructions: Write just the number of minutes, without the unit.

questions.prompt: Six numbers have a mean of 15. Five of them total 71. What is the sixth number?
questions.explanation: The required total is 6 × 15 = 90; 90 − 71 = 19.

questions.prompt: A 2.75 m rope has 35 cm cut off. How many centimetres remain?
questions.explanation: Two point seven five metres is 275 cm; subtract 35 cm to leave 240.
questions.instructions: Write just the number of centimetres, without the unit.

questions.prompt: Start with a number, subtract 5, multiply by 4, then add 2 to get 62. What was the number?
Which TWO numbers have exactly three factors?
questions.explanation: Squares of primes have exactly three factors; 9 is 3² and 25 is 5².

questions.prompt: Which TWO expressions equal 1 1/2?
questions.explanation: Three halves and nine sixths both equal one and a half.

metadata.subject: numeracy
metadata.skill: Match improper fractions to a mixed number

questions.prompt: Which TWO statements describe a translation of a shape?

options.text: Every point moves the same distance
The shape turns around a point
The shape becomes a mirror image

questions.explanation: A translation slides every point equally and preserves size and orientation.

questions.prompt: A number rounds to 4,500 to the nearest hundred. Which TWO could it be?
questions.explanation: Values from 4,450 through 4,549 round to 4,500, so 4,451 and 4,549 fit.

questions.prompt: Order these decimals from greatest to least.
questions.explanation: Writing hundredths gives 1.90, 1.19, 1.09 and 0.99.

questions.prompt: Order these areas from smallest to largest.
questions.explanation: One square metre is 10,000 cm², so the values are 20,000, 15,000, 25,000 and 10,000 cm².

questions.prompt: Order the steps for using a scale of 1 cm represents 4 km to find the real distance of a 7.5 cm map route.
questions.explanation: Read the scale, measure the route, multiply by four kilometres per centimetre, then state 30 km.

questions.prompt: Order the operations that correctly evaluate 5 + 3 × (12 − 8) ÷ 2.
questions.explanation: Brackets come first, then multiplication and division from left to right, and addition last.
